data.name: Anulata
data.gender_notes: Anulata is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Anulata means 'desire' or 'attraction'. It is derived from the Sanskrit root word 'anu' which means 'towards' and 'lata' which means 'that which is drawn towards'. In Hindu mythology, Anulata represents the deep-rooted emotions and longings of the heart. The name Anulata carries the meaning “Desire, attraction, love” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Anulata usually hope their child will grow to embody desire, attraction, love and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes deep emotional connection and love
data.etymology: Anulata belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Desire, attraction, love.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Anulata total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

It is also widely used as a female name in Hindu communities. In Indian literature and art, the concept of Anulata is often depicted as the driving force behind the actions and desires of individuals, symbolizing both love and longing.

historical_references.reference: Anulata, the goddess of love and fertility, was an important deity in the Shakta tradition of Hinduism. She was often depicted as a beautiful, voluptuous woman with multiple arms and the ability to bestow children upon childless couples. Anulata is believed to have originated from the Tantric texts of the medieval period.
